findings.title: Client hook throws plain Error on non-2xx, losing ApiError contract
findings.rationale: The new useDismissAllSuggestions mutation calls fetch directly and, on a non-2xx response, does not read the server's { error: { code, message, details } } body and does not throw ApiError. It returns res.json() unconditionally, which on an error response either throws a generic Error (if the body is not JSON) or returns the error body as data. Per rule 3, every client request must surface errors as ApiError so pages can show the server's message, status, and code. This breaks the contract for the findings panel's error handling.

findings.title: Client error handling bypasses ApiError contract
findings.rationale: The new useDismissAllSuggestions hook calls fetch directly and, on a non-2xx response, throws a plain Error (or returns the error body as data). This violates house rule 3: client requests must surface errors as ApiError so pages can show the server's message, status, and code. The server returns 204 with no body on success, so res.json() on a 204 will throw a SyntaxError, and on error the server's { error: { code, message, details } } body is parsed as data instead of being converted to ApiError. The FindingsPanel will show a generic error message and lose the status and code.

findings.title: Missing res.ok check on fetch response
findings.rationale: The mutationFn does not check res.ok before calling res.json(). On a 204 success the body is empty, so res.json() throws a SyntaxError that is not converted to ApiError. On a 4xx/5xx the error body is parsed as data and returned as the mutation result, so the caller cannot distinguish success from failure and the error is silently swallowed (onSuccess will run with the error body as data). This is a correctness defect that breaks the panel's refresh-on-success behavior.

findings.title: Client mutation throws plain Error on non-2xx, breaking ApiError contract
findings.rationale: The new useDismissAllSuggestions mutation calls fetch directly and, on a non-2xx response, does not read the error body or throw ApiError. Per api-contract-house-rules #3, client code under client/src/ that calls the engine with fetch directly must, on non-2xx, throw ApiError (with code/message/details from the error body) or return the error body as data. Here, a 4xx/5xx response will cause res.json() to throw a plain SyntaxError (or the caller gets a generic error), losing the server's error code and message. The findings panel will show a generic error instead of the server's message.

findings.title: 204 No Content response breaks client res.json() call
findings.rationale: The server route returns reply.code(204) with no body (server/src/modules/reviews/routes.ts:153-155). The client mutation calls res.json() on that response. A 204 No Content response has no body; calling res.json() on it rejects with a SyntaxError ("Unexpected end of JSON input"). This means every successful bulk-dismiss will throw in the mutation, the onSuccess callback (which invalidates the findings query) will never run, and the panel will not refresh. The user sees no error (the mutation rejects) but the UI does not update, and the error is swallowed or surfaces as a generic failure.

findings.title: New route not added to shared contract copies
findings.rationale: The new POST /pulls/:id/findings/dismiss-suggestions route is added to the server routes but the shared contract files (server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts and client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts) are not updated to include this route. Per api-contract-house-rules #2, a shared contract change must be made in both copies in the same diff. The client's typed API layer (if it uses the shared contract) will not know about this route, and the two copies will drift. Even though the route is new (not a change to an existing field), the contract files should document it so the client's type-safe API surface stays in sync.

findings.rationale: The new `POST /pulls/:id/findings/dismiss-suggestions` route is added to the server, but the corresponding client contract (in `client/src/vendor/shared/`) is not updated. Per house rule 2, a shared contract change must be mirrored in both copies. The client's `useDismissAllSuggestions` hardcodes the URL string instead of using a shared contract type, so the two copies will silently drift. This is a WARNING because existing callers keep working, but the contract is now inconsistent.

findings.title: Missing error handling in client mutation: non-2xx responses not surfaced as ApiError
findings.rationale: The `useDismissAllSuggestions` hook does not check `res.ok` before calling `res.json()`. On a 4xx/5xx response, the server returns a JSON error body, but the hook will either throw a SyntaxError (if the body is empty, e.g., 204) or return the error body as data, which the caller will treat as success. This violates house rule 3 and the caller will not show the server's error message or code.

matched_title: Client mutation swallows HTTP errors and treats failures as success

findings.title: Client mutation swallows HTTP errors and treats failures as success
findings.rationale: The new useDismissAllSuggestions mutationFn calls fetch directly and returns res.json() without checking res.ok. On a non-2xx response (e.g. 422 from a schema violation, 500 from the server), res.json() parses the error body and returns it as the mutation's data. The onSuccess callback then runs, invalidating the reviews query and refreshing the panel — so a failed bulk-dismiss looks like a success and the panel shows stale data. This violates rule 3 (client requests surface errors as ApiError): the code should use apiFetch, which throws ApiError on non-2xx, or explicitly check res.ok and throw new ApiError(message, res.status, code, details) reading code/message/details from the error body. The caller that breaks is the findings panel: a reviewer who clicks 'Dismiss all suggestions' and gets a 422/500 will see the panel refresh as if the dismiss succeeded, with no error surfaced.

findings.title: New route not added to shared contract copies — server and client contract drift
findings.rationale: The new POST /pulls/:id/findings/dismiss-suggestions route is added to the server routes but not to either copy of the shared contract (server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts and client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts). Rule 2 says a shared contract change must be made in both copies in the same diff. Here the route is a new endpoint that the client will call; without adding it to the shared contract, the two copies now disagree on the API surface. The client's useDismissAllSuggestions hook calls the endpoint, but the contract files don't declare it, so any type-checking or codegen that consumes the contract will not know the route exists — and the client and server contract definitions silently drift. The caller that breaks is any consumer of the shared contract (e.g. the client's typed API layer, or a codegen step) that now has an undeclared route. Compatible alternative: add the route to both copies of the shared contract in this same diff, or, if the contract files are not meant to enumerate routes, document the route in the shared contract's route list so the copies stay in sync.

matched_title: Client mutation throws plain Error, breaking ApiError contract

findings.title: Client mutation throws plain Error, breaking ApiError contract
findings.rationale: The new useDismissAllSuggestions mutation calls fetch directly and, on a non-2xx response, throws a plain Error (the fetch promise rejects with a TypeError). This violates rule 3: client code under client/src/ that calls the engine with fetch directly must throw ApiError on non-2xx so pages can surface the server's error code/message. The existing useFindingAction hook (line 156) uses apiFetch and correctly throws ApiError. The new code breaks the contract for any caller that catches ApiError to show the server's message — they now get a generic error and lose the status and code. The caller that breaks is the FindingsPanel component (FindingsPanel.tsx) which relies on ApiError to display the server's error message when the bulk-dismiss fails (e.g., 401/403/500). Compatible alternative: use apiFetch (or the existing apiFetch wrapper) which already builds ApiError from the server's { error: { code, message, details } } body, and return the parsed JSON on success. The current code also calls res.json() on a 204 No Content response, which will throw a SyntaxError (no JSON body) — another plain Error that breaks the contract.

findings.title: New route missing from server shared contract copy
findings.rationale: The new POST /pulls/:id/findings/dismiss-suggestions route is added to the server's routes.ts but the corresponding contract definition (the route path, method, params schema, and response type) is not added to server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts (or the shared contracts file that documents the API surface). Rule 2 requires that a shared contract change appears in both copies in the same diff. The server's shared contract copy is canonical; the client's copy is a hand copy. Since the route is new, the server's shared contract copy must be updated to document it, and the client's copy must be updated to match. Without this, the client's type definitions (which are generated from the shared contract) will not know about the new endpoint, and any type-safe client call will fail to compile or silently drift. The caller that breaks is the client's type-safe API layer (e.g., client/src/lib/api.ts or the generated types) which relies on the shared contract to know the route exists. Compatible alternative: add the route definition to both copies of the shared contract (server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts and client/src/vendor/shared/contracts/findings.ts) in this same diff, including the params schema (IdParams) and the 204 response type.

findings.title: Duplicate tag keys in React list
findings.rationale: The new `tags.map((tag) => <span key={tag}>...)` uses the tag string as the React key. If a finding ever contains duplicate tags (the contract does not forbid duplicates), React will warn about duplicate keys and may mis-render. Using the index or deduping tags would be more robust.
